import re def find_html_tags(html_content: str) -> list[str]: """ Return a list of all HTML tags found in the input string. Parameters ---------- html_content : str A string containing HTML content to be parsed. Returns ------- list[str] List of matched tag strings, e.g. ['
', '

', '']. Notes ----- * The function uses a non-greedy regular expression that matches any sequence starting with '<', ending with '>', and not containing a newline in between. * It is deliberately simple and does not attempt to validate tag syntax or handle malformed HTML. This keeps the function fast and safe from complex regex backtracking issues. * Any exception during processing is caught and an empty list is returned, ensuring the function never raises. """ try: # Match tags: start with '<', then any characters except '>' (non-greedy), # until the first '>'. This will capture self-closing tags as well. pattern = r'<[^>]+>' return re.findall(pattern, html_content) except Exception: # In case of any unforeseen error, return an empty list. return []
